seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: June to mid-July, while snow still bridges the creek valley and the glacier's crevasses before they open up

May.reason: Firm snow runs from the road-end clearcut to the glacier, but spring avalanche cycles off the Hanging Glacier and basin slopes are still active.

June.reason: Deep snow still fills the creek valley and bridges most crevasses, so the approach avoids slide alder; cross under the Hanging Glacier early.

July.reason: Snow recedes from the valley bottom and the clearcut contour gets brushier, but crevasses on the White Salmon are usually still bridged early in the month.

August.reason: The approach becomes a brushy contour with stream crossings, and crevasses on the White Salmon and Curtis glaciers open, lengthening route-finding.

September.reason: Bare, broken glacier and open crevasses make travel slow and circuitous, and the summit pyramid scramble is looser once snow is gone.

October.reason: Shortening days, first autumn snow over open crevasses, and wet brush on the approach make this a poor time for the glacier.

evidence: Search summaries: White Salmon is the most popular winter/spring SKI route on Shuksan; Jan 2026 WTA report warns avalanche danger on the glacier and basin can be extreme - https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/trip-reports/trip_report-2026-01-24.215020785095
Turns-all-year reports on the White Salmon in March, April and May (firm snow May 2) - https://turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/may-2-white-salmon-glacier-mt-shuksan

Kyle Miller early-June ascent: rollers and crevasses hidden under 10+ ft of snow; an hour of bushwhacking snowless forest on the descent - https://www.whereiskylemiller.com/mt-baker-542/white-salmon-glacier/

Row's own approach text: with good snow cover descend into White Salmon Creek; without it contour the clearcut to avoid slide alder; hazards list Hanging Glacier avalanches and worse crevasses late season.
flags: Research shows this is heavily used as a winter/spring (March-May) ski-mountaineering line; the stored season Jun-Sep reflects the summer climbing window only. Breakdown stays inside Jun-Sep for optimal/good and marks May marginal.

Could not verify any specific seasonal closure for the White Salmon Lodge road-end pull-off; the access.seasonal note about Baker Lake Road (FSR 11) applies to the Sulphide/Shannon Ridge side, not this Mount Baker Highway approach - worth a human look.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Mid-July to mid-August, when the snow and ice leading to the ridge are consolidated and the rock has melted out

June.reason: The north-side snow and ice below the ridge climb well early in the morning, but the upper rock is often still snow-plastered and wet.

July.reason: Glacier approaches below the ridge are consolidated and the 4th class to 5.7 rock melts out; bergschrund crossings are usually still manageable.

August.reason: Rock on the summit block is driest, though the ice lower down grows harder and more serac and crevasse obstacles appear by late month.

September.reason: Bare glacier ice, wide bergschrunds and serac fall on the north-side approach make reaching the base of the ridge hard and exposed.

evidence: StephAbegg North Face trip, June 9 2013: 40-50 degree firm snow early, would turn dangerous within hours of sun - https://stephabegg.com/trip-reports/washington/shuksan-nf/

SummitPost Shuksan climber's log: early August relaxed conditions; earlier-season gullies with wet mixed snow/ice/rock are a challenge; serac fall destroyed an easy exit, forcing traverses above an open bergschrund - https://www.summitpost.org/mount-shuksan/climbers-log/150347/d-13302
Row's own best_season (Jul-Aug, consolidated glacier terrain and rock) and beta (ice lower down, alpine rock higher up).
flags: Few trip reports exist for this specific line; month statuses are inferred from north-side (North Face / Hanging Glacier) conditions plus the stored Jul-Aug window. Worth a human look.
Row has no hazards and its approach depends on another route; June/September assessments rely on that connecting terrain.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Mid-July through August, after the Boulder Ridge snow retreats and before the Park Glacier becomes too broken

May.reason: Continuous snow reaches far down Boulder Ridge, making a long slog, and the east-facing cleaver carries more rockfall as the snowpack warms.

June.reason: Deep snow still buries the upper trail and heather step, and warming slopes below the 9,300 ft buttress shed more rock.

July.reason: The trail melts out to high camp near 5,700 ft and snow still bridges most Park Glacier crevasses; expect flies and blowdown on the lower trail.

August.reason: The approach is fully melted out, but the glacier grows broken and the upper cleaver turns icy, so later trips need screws and careful routing.

September.reason: The Park Glacier is heavily crevassed and the cleaver steep, icy and exposed to rockfall; parties have needed screws and pickets.

evidence: Turns-all-year July 15-16 2009: continuous snow from summit to 4,700 ft on Boulder Ridge in mid-July - https://turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/july-15-16-2009-mt-baker-via-boulder-glacier
Turns-all-year July 22-23: bushwhack approach with biting black flies, mud and blowdown - https://www.turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/july-22-23-boulder-glacier-mt-baker

Eric's Basecamp, Sept 7-8 2001: multiple crevasse fields on the Park Glacier; upper cleaver steep, icy, exposed to rockfall, protected with screws and pickets - http://ericsbasecamp.net/trips/Boulder-Park/Boulder-Park.htm
Row's own best_season: mid-July through August; June too early, September too broken.
flags: Stored season is May-Aug, but the row's own best_season says June is too early; May/June are therefore marked marginal, not good. September sits outside the stored window and is marked risky, consistent with best_season.
access.seasonal mentions Baker Lake Road (FSR 11) bridge-work closures - no specific current closure dates verified.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late May through June, while snow still covers the approach and before the bergschrund near 9,400 ft opens

April.reason: Snow still blocks the road about two miles short of the trailhead, adding distance, and spring avalanche cycles are still active on the open slopes.

May.reason: Continuous snow from near the trailhead to the summit and a filled-in bergschrund; the last stretch of road may still hold snow early in the month.

June.reason: The road is usually clear and crevasses remain bridged, though some sag late in the month and need to be walked around.

July.reason: Still climbable early in the month, but the bergschrund above the Squak-Easton junction becomes convoluted and more crevasses open.

August.reason: The bergschrund near 9,400 ft and open crevasses force detours, and many parties switch to the Easton Glacier instead.

evidence: Squak is limited to early season because a bergschrund develops as the season progresses - https://www.alpineinstitute.com/articles/summit-mt-baker-your-guide-to-the-easton-squak-and-coleman-deming-routes/

Turns-all-year Aug 25 2012: bergschrund at 9,400 ft after Squak/Easton join becoming convoluted but still passable - https://turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/august-25-2012-mt-baker-easton-and-squak-glaciers
June 2023 report: crevasses on the Squak sagging and about to open - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/mt-baker-squak-glacier-one-day-ski-mountaineering

Winter road blocked ~2 miles from trailhead; May report found snow on the road ~2.8 miles out - search summary of https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/schriebers-meadow-snowshoe and https://www.turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/squak-glacier-mt-baker-5-23-24
flags: Stored season May-Jul (early season preferred) matches research. August is outside the window and is marked marginal; an August 2012 report found the schrund still passable, so August is possible but not recommended.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: May, while the south-facing couloir is still full and firm overnight, before rockfall and Nisqually crevasses take over

March.reason: Deep winter snowpack fills the couloir, but storm cycles, short days and the nightly Longmire-Paradise gate make windows rare and avalanche-prone.

April.reason: The couloir is fat with snow and Nisqually crevasses are well bridged; fresh spring storms still load the south aspect, so time it after a freeze.

May.reason: Firm refrozen snow in the couloir and bridged crevasses on the Nisqually crossing; start around midnight to be off the south face before it warms.

June.reason: Still climbable early in the month, but rockfall down the narrow couloir rises as it melts and crevasses on the Nisqually crossing begin to open.

July.reason: In most years the couloir is melting out: heavy rockfall down the funnel, a broken Nisqually crossing and wet-snow slides by mid-morning.

evidence: Sister Fuhrer Finger 'typically goes out in early June due to rockfall and crevasses opening on the Nisqually'; late June/early July only in big snow years - https://www.powderproject.com/trail/7000332/fuhrer-finger (via search summary)
Fuhrer Thumb descent in mid/late May with high-season snowpack; crevasses to cross once melting starts - https://www.whereiskylemiller.com/mt-rainier/fuhrer-thumb/
Rockfall hazard high after sunrise; south side parties leave ~midnight - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/intermediate-alpine-climb-mount-rainier-fuhrer-finger
Fuhrer Finger ski June 25-26 2010 in May-like conditions (high snow year) - https://turns-all-year.com/trip-reports/june-25-26-2010-mt-rainier-fuhrer-finger
flags: Evidence here is mostly for the adjacent Fuhrer Finger; Thumb-specific month data is thin. Breakdown agrees with stored Apr-Jun but rates late June weaker than the stored window implies.
Row's access.permit says 'Free climbing permit' while access.fees states an $82 climbing fee - internal contradiction worth a look (not seasonal).

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July, when the headwall holds firm neve and the Mowich approach is snow-free, before the bergschrund becomes impassable

May.reason: The Mowich Lake road is still closed and snowed in, adding many miles, and the northwest face carries unconsolidated spring snow and slide risk.

June.reason: The face is well filled and corns up for ski descents, but the Mowich Lake road usually has not opened and the approach through Spray Park is snowbound.

July.reason: Firm neve on the headwall and a melted-out approach; the bergschrund may need a bypass on climber's left, and rockfall picks up once sun hits the face.

August.reason: The bergschrund grows and the face turns to penitentes and hard ice, with more rockfall and wider crevasses on the Edmunds approach.

September.reason: Late-season bare ice and open crevasses on a remote face, with the first fall storms arriving and shortening days.

evidence: Ranger conditions July 25 2017: main bergschrund impassable, bypass on left near twin gendarme; firm neve with penitentes; rockfall - https://mountrainierclimbing.blogspot.com/2017/07/edmunds-headwall-mowich-face-route.html
Headwall often skied June/July when it corns up - https://wildsnow.com/10311/rainier-edmunds-headwall-ski/
Mowich Lake Road open to vehicles typically mid-July to mid-October - https://www.nps.gov/places/mowich-lake.htm
SR 165 Fairfax Bridge closed April 2025, no alternate route to Mowich Lake - https://wsdot.wa.gov/about/news/2025/103-year-old-sr-165-carbon-river-fairfax-bridge-permanently-closed
flags: Access blocker: the SR 165 Fairfax Bridge closure means no vehicle access to the Mowich Lake trailhead in ANY month until further notice; the month breakdown describes the route itself, not current access. Consider whether guidance should mention it.
Stored window Jun-Jul, but the Mowich Lake road normally opens only in mid-July, so a June attempt implies a long snowbound approach; reasons say so rather than contradict the window.
Row's access.permit calls the climbing permit 'Free' while access.fees states $82 - internal contradiction (not seasonal).

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late June through July, while the snow finger still bridges onto the glacier and the upper moat is crossable

May.reason: Snow on the upper Cle Elum road and over Dip Top Gap lengthens the approach, and loaded slopes above Marmot and Jade Lakes are avalanche terrain.

June.reason: The snow finger right of Pea Soup Lake gives a direct line onto the glacier past the lower icefall, and the moat below the col is still well filled.

July.reason: The approach is mostly melted out and the finger usually still goes early in the month; the moat starts to open and mosquitoes are heavy below 6,500 ft.

August.reason: The finger breaks up, forcing a Class 3 bypass on loose rock; crevasses can span the glacier and crossing the upper moat becomes the crux.

September.reason: Bare, broken ice and a wide moat under the col, with loose rotten rock to reach the glacier; some years the lower route does not go at all.

evidence: Early season snow finger on far right bypasses lower icefall; late season Class 3 scramble left of finger - https://www.mountainproject.com/route/124973025/lynch-glacier (via search summary)

Moat crossing below the pyramid tricky; 2023 simple up high, impassable down low - Mountaineers trip reports (search summary) https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/glacier-climb-mount-daniel-lynch-glacier-2
Late season: full-width crevasses, loose rock access, Lynch Draw flooded - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/mount-daniel-lynch-glacier (403, search summary)

Trip reports dated 6/28/2008 and 7/6/2020 - https://cascadeclimbers.com/forum/topic/60321-tr-mt-daniel-lynch-glacier-6282008/ , https://cascadeclimbers.com/forum/topic/103525-tr-mt-daniel-daniel-and-lynch-glaciers-07062020/
flags: Agrees with stored Jun-Jul. Cle Elum River road / Deception Pass trailhead opening date not verified, stated generally.
Row's high_point_ft is null (not seasonal).

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: April to May, when the couloir is continuously snow-filled and the Eightmile road is about to open or has just opened

February.reason: Fully snow-filled, but the Eightmile road is gated and snowbound, adding miles of road approach, with short days and winter avalanche cycles.

March.reason: Deep, filling couloir, but the road gate is still closed and storm loading at the top raises cornice and slab concerns.

April.reason: Consolidating spring snow the whole way up; the road is still gated so expect a long walk in, but the lake is frozen and easy to cross.

May.reason: The Eightmile road often opens in late spring, cutting the approach; lake ice breaks up about then, and overnight permits apply from May 15.

June.reason: Still mostly snow, but sun-warmed rock above sheds more debris; overnight camps at the lake need the Enchantment permit lottery.

July.reason: Short Class 4 rock steps melt out in the couloir, the snow softens fast, and rockfall and ice debris increase.

August.reason: The couloir is largely bare, with loose rock steps and a broken descent over the Colchuck Glacier.

evidence: Most often climbed in winter or early spring while the couloir is entirely filled; Eightmile road may be snowed in and/or gated then - https://www.summitpost.org/north-buttress-couloir/162206 (403, search summary)

Early May trip: road closed at Bridge Creek, +8 mi road walking; rangers said it would open by permit season; another report Eightmile Road open 5/15 - Mountaineers trip reports via search, https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/colchuck-peak-north-buttress-couloir-3
Colchuck Lake ice starts breaking up around mid-May on an average year - https://spokalpine.com/2016/04/11/colchuck-peak/ (search summary)
Late summer Class 4 rock exposed - row beta; https://wenatcheeoutdoors.org/2016/07/16/colchuck-north-buttress-couloir/
flags: Research says the route is often climbed in winter as well; stored window starts at March. February is included as a marginal shoulder, not rated good, to stay consistent with the stored Mar-Jun.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: February to March, after a cold clear night, when the gully is filled and firm and the sunny half has not yet turned to slush

December.reason: At this low elevation the gully is often not yet filled in, leaving rock and brush exposed, and early storm snow sits unconsolidated on the slope below.

January.reason: The gully is usually filled, but new storm snow loads it quickly and daylight is short; climb only after a stable forecast and a cold, clear night.

February.reason: Deep, settled snowpack fills the gully to the ridge; the shaded half stays firm, though a cornice often builds at the exit.

March.reason: Freeze-thaw cycles firm the snow for step-kicking early in the day; start early before sun softens the exposed half and wet slides begin.

April.reason: The sun-exposed half turns to slush by mid-morning, with wet slides and rollerballs, and the lower gully starts to melt out at this elevation.

May.reason: The gully melts out into rock and wet snow with wet-slab and cornice-collapse hazard; by summer it is no longer a snow climb.

evidence: January through April have the best winter conditions on Guye's gullies; avalanches common in bad conditions; resort blasting on the south flank - https://www.summitpost.org/guye-peak/150942 (search summary)
1973 accident in the Southeast Gully on March 25: frozen snow, step cutting, trees for belays - http://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/13197302400
flags: Agrees with stored Jan-Apr; April rated marginal rather than good because of wet-slide warming the row's own best_season describes.
Row's best_season names NWAC as the forecast to check - the agency is named as a thing to consult, which may or may not fall foul of the no-sources rule (not seasonal_guidance text).

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July, while seasonal snow still covers the Colchuck Glacier to the col and before it melts to hard bare ice

June.reason: The access road may still be closed and the glacier gully holds deep, avalanche-prone snow; the scramble ridge above the col can still be snow-covered.

July.reason: Continuous consolidated snow up the glacier to the col takes crampons well, and the Class 2-3 ridge above is mostly melted out.

August.reason: Snow on the glacier thins and gets suncupped; patches of hard ice near the col become more likely late in the month, so crampons are essential.

September.reason: Seasonal snow is often gone, leaving bare glacier ice at the 40-degree section below the col where crampons bite poorly and a slip is hard to stop.

October.reason: Fresh snow over bare glacier ice, short days and freezing temperatures make the glacier and col treacherous; the access road can close with the first heavy snow.

evidence: Colchuck Glacier transitions to bare/blue ice once the current year's snow melts; late season not recommended - https://www.summitpost.org/colchuck-glacier/162204 and https://besthikesbc.ca/hiking-colchuck-peak-in-the-enchantments/
Early July 2026 report: snow coverage continuous on climber's right of the glacier - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/alpine-scramble-colchuck-peak-east-route
Early-season ascents (June) common on Colchuck Glacier - https://northwestadventurejournal.wordpress.com/2026/06/22/colchuck-peak-6-7-26/
FR 7601 closes in winter, roughly Nov-May - https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/lake-stuart
flags: Stored best_season (late July through September) disagrees with evidence: the Colchuck Glacier approach to the col is best on snow (June-July) and turns to bare ice by late August/September, so September is marked marginal, not good.
Research suggests June ascents are common and often better on snow, but June is outside the stored Jul-Oct season; it is marked marginal only. A human may want to widen the window to Jun-Sep.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July to August, once the snow finger and moat at the base shrink and the northwest-facing granite is dry

June.reason: The snowfield to the base needs crampons and axe, and the moat between snow and rock can be awkward to cross; the access road may not yet be open.

July.reason: The moraine approach melts out and the snow finger shrinks, though early July may still need crampons for the last few hundred feet to the base.

August.reason: Driest, warmest rock and the least snow on the approach; long days suit the Grade IV length, but start early to beat afternoon thunderstorms.

September.reason: Dry, stable rock with fewer storms, but shorter days make a single-push ascent tighter and the northwest face stays cold in the morning.

October.reason: Short days, cold shaded rock and the first snowfalls can glaze ledges and the upper gully; the access road can close with the first heavy snow.

evidence: Multiple June ascents (2009, June 8 2017, June 2019) with moat and snow at base - https://spokalpine.com/2017/07/13/dragontail-peak-serpentine-arete-iv-5-8/ and https://climberkyle.com/2019/06/15/dragontail-peak-serpentine-arete-5-8/
July 2005 party cramponed up the last few hundred feet of snowfield to the base; 7/8/2017 TR - https://cascadeclimbers.com/forum/topic/100805-tr-dragontail-peak-serpentine-arete-782017/
FR 7601 closes in winter, roughly Nov-May - https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/lake-stuart
flags: June ascents are well documented (moat and snow at the base, crampons needed), but June is outside the stored Jul-Oct season; it is marked marginal only.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Mid-July to August, when the north-facing rock is driest and the descent gully has mostly melted out

June.reason: Snow slopes on the approach and a steep, possibly corniced descent notch toward Aasgard Pass; the north-facing rock is often wet and cold.

July.reason: Approach snow shrinks and the ridge dries out; early in the month crampons and an axe are still useful for the snow slope and the descent.

August.reason: Driest rock and longest days for this long Grade IV ridge; firm snow may linger on the descent, and afternoon thunderstorms are a threat on the Fin.

September.reason: Rock remains dry, but shorter days tighten the schedule and the shaded north aspect stays cold; descent snow may be hard and icy.

October.reason: Early snow and verglas on the north-facing ridge and short days make the long route and descent slow; the access road can close with the first heavy snow.

evidence: Descent toward Aasgard on moderately steep, sometimes very firm snow; early-season notch steep and possibly corniced - https://www.summitpost.org/dragontail-backbone-ridge-to-the-fin/539545

Route guide and trip reports - https://guidedexposure.com/blogs/guided-exposure-blog/backbone-ridge-on-dragontail-peak-a-complete-route-guide , https://www.jeffreyjhebert.com/adventures/backbone-ridge-on-dragontail-peak
FR 7601 closes in winter, roughly Nov-May - https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/lake-stuart

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July to September, after the snow clears from Ingalls Pass and the basin and the loose upper face is dry

June.reason: Snow and ice linger near Ingalls Pass and throughout the basin, and the ledges to the ridge can be snow-covered; Lake Ingalls may still be frozen.

July.reason: Snow melts off Ingalls Pass and the ledges to the ridge base through the month; early July may still need care on snow patches.

August.reason: Dry rock matters most on the runout, loose upper east-face pitch; the approach is snow-free, though afternoon thunderstorms are common.

September.reason: Stable, dry weather and cooler temperatures; larch season late in the month brings heavy crowds to the trail and trailhead.

October.reason: Early snow or ice on the poorly protected upper face turns a 5.6 X pitch dangerous, and days are short.

evidence: Lake Ingalls/Ingalls Pass: lingering snow and ice near the pass; July-September best, June and October may have snow and a frozen lake; late July recommended - https://explorewithalec.com/lake-ingalls/ , https://www.10adventures.com/hikes/wenatchee-national-forest/lake-ingalls-hike/
June trip report: snow throughout the basin - https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/trip-reports/trip_report.2017-06-21.4668538392
East Peak route character - https://www.summitpost.org/ingalls-peaks/151160
flags: Could not verify the North Fork Teanaway Road opening date, so reasons avoid naming one.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July to late August, once the arete is snow-free and before the glacier traverse to its base turns to bare ice

June.reason: Cascade River Road is often still gated short of the trailhead, and wet approach snow and snow-filled gullies keep the loose arete out of shape.

July.reason: Road open and glaciers still well bridged, but early July can leave snow in the chimneys and gullies; late July is usually dry.

August.reason: Rock is fully dry and days are long enough for the 17-hour climb, though crevasses on the traverse below the west face are opening.

September.reason: The Eldorado and Inspiration glaciers go to bare ice with open crevasses and moats, and shorter days raise the odds of a forced bivy.

October.reason: Short days, early snow and rime on a loose 19-pitch route, and the Cascade River Road can close with the first storms or washouts.

evidence: NPS Eldorado conditions blog: June approach snow 4,000-5,300 ft; Jul-Aug crevasses and bergschrunds opening; Sept blue ice, very visible crevasses - https://www.nps.gov/noca/blogs/climbing-conditions-for-eldorado-area.htm
Spokalpine TR 26 Jul 2025: 17 h round trip from base camp, summited at sunset, mid-season snow-free timing - https://spokalpine.com/2025/07/30/eldorado-peak-west-arete-iv-5-8/
CascadeClimbers TR titles show ascents 7/26/2025 and 9/24/2012 - https://cascadeclimbers.com/forum/topic/88711-tr-eldorado-west-arete-9242012/

Late-season Inspiration Glacier: bridges scarce, moats along rocks, crevasses parallel to ridge - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/north-cascades-national-park-cross-country-zones/high-occupancy-xc-zones/eldorado-peak-inspiration-glacier
flags: Stored season is Jul-Aug but best_season prose says roughly July-September; a documented 24 Sep 2012 ascent supports September as possible, so it is marked marginal (outside the stored window) rather than good.

access.closures says the road is closed roughly Nov-June at mile 20 while best_season says often not accessible until late June - consistent, but the exact gate timing varies by year and could not be verified.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: August to early September, when the approach gully has melted out and the gneiss ridge is dry, before autumn rime arrives

June.reason: The Thornton Lakes Road is unmaintained and may hold snow or downed trees, and the approach gully and glacier remnant are still deep in snow.

July.reason: Snow still fills the approach gully and basin below the ridge, easing travel but with a growing moat and thin snowbridges to cross.

August.reason: The ridge is dry and the gully mostly melted out, though the loose scree gully to the col becomes a tedious grind with heavy packs.

September.reason: Early September is snow-free on the talus approach and dry on the ridge; water at the col may mean melting snow, and days shorten.

October.reason: First snow and rime make the exposed gneiss ridge and long rappel descent unsafe, and short days leave little margin.

evidence: StephAbegg TR 1-3 Sep 2006: much less snow than historic; approach was 1,200 ft of loose talus/grass; melt snow for water at col; col quota ~2 parties - https://stephabegg.com/trip-reports/washington/triumph-ne-ridge/

July TRs: moat forming mid-traverse requiring a jump, thin snowbridge into the gully to the NE ridge notch - https://cascadeclimbers.com/forum/topic/107842-tr-mount-triumph-ne-ridge-07132024/ ; https://havetent.com/2022/07/19/mt-triumph-ne-ridge/
Thornton Lakes Road rough, not plowed or maintained in winter; trailhead sits west of the SR 20 winter gate - https://www.cynhw.com/blog/2021/2/22/thornton-lakes
Spokalpine TR dated Oct 2024 post (climb date not verified) - https://spokalpine.com/2024/10/05/triumph-ne-ridge-iii-5-7/
flags: No disagreement with stored Jul-Sep window. Water availability at the col in late season is inferred from a single report.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July through August, after the ridge rock sheds its snow and while the glacier approach still holds consolidated snow

June.reason: SR 20 is usually open by now and snow eases the Burgundy Col descent, but the northeast-facing rock still holds snow and ice.

July.reason: Firm morning snow on the glacier and snowfield below the Chianti Spires, with the ridge drying out through the month.

August.reason: Rock is dry and the glacier still mostly snow-covered, though the Burgundy Col gully turns to loose scree as its snow melts.

September.reason: Dry rock, but the glacier shows more ice and open cracks, and melted-out boulder fields make the approach slower.

October.reason: Early storms plaster the northeast aspect and can close SR 20 for the season, and short days hurt a long glacier-plus-rock day.

evidence: Mountaineers glacier TR June 2025: no snow on climbers trail to Burgundy Col, soft consolidated snow on backside, bullet-proof snow at dawn - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/basic-glacier-climb-silver-star-mountain-silver-star-glacier

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July and August, when the Sloan Glacier is well bridged and the corkscrew ledges have melted free of snow

May.reason: The Mountain Loop Highway gate often has not opened and deep snow on the approach and ledges brings avalanche and route-finding problems.

June.reason: Consolidated snow from mid elevations slows route-finding, drainages run high, and the upper ledges may still hold snow.

July.reason: The glacier is sealed with solid snow bridges and a clear boot path, and the upper west-face ledges come free of snow.

August.reason: Ledges and summit scramble are dry, but by late August the glacier breaks up and crevasses need weaving around.

September.reason: Crevasses widen on the Sloan Glacier and the crossing can become impassable sometime this month; check recent conditions first.

evidence: Mountaineers TRs: July 2026 solid snow bridges and boot path, FR 4096 improved; June 2022 consolidated snow slowed route-finding 3.6-4.8k ft; late Aug 2016 glacier pretty broken up - https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/sloan-peak-corkscrew-route-c2c-via-bedel-creek

July-August safest; glacier typically impassable sometime in September - https://engineeredforadventure.com/sloan/ ; https://rocknropenw.com/2024/08/02/sloan-peak-corkscrew-route-from-bedal-trailhead/
Mountain Loop Highway typically reopens mid-May; some years not until June - https://townofdarrington.com/mountain-loop-highway-open/
flags: Stored season 'Jun-Sep (best Jul-Aug)' and best_season 'late June through August' agree with evidence; June and September are marked marginal because early June snow and September glacier breakup make them less than good.
Row has grade null and is a duplicate of the Corkscrew Route per its own beta; worth a human look.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: August to September, once the north-face ledge traverse is snow-free and before fall storms close the road

May.reason: The Mountain Loop Highway gate may still be closed, and deep snow lingers on Headlee Pass and the north-face ledges.

June.reason: Steep, exposed snow still covers the heather ledge traverse and the upper route, needing ice axe and crampons.

July.reason: The route rock is dry, but lingering snow on the approach ledges can leave a moat to scramble through at the base.

August.reason: Approach ledges usually melt out, leaving dry granite and long days; weekends get crowded on the six pitches.

September.reason: Snow-free ledges and dry rock, though loose stacked blocks on pitch 4 are a known rockfall risk late season.

October.reason: Still climbed in dry spells, but short days, cold on the north face, and first snow that closes the road make it a gamble.
